memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Have Aaron your brother brought to you from among the Israelites, along with his sons Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, so they may serve me as priests." - Exodus 28:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God calls Aaron and his sons out from among the Israelites to serve as priests. Notice that phrase — "from among." They were not a different kind of people. They came from the same families, shared the same weaknesses, walked the same camp. What set them apart was not superior character but God's calling.

That matters, because we sometimes imagine that God chooses people who have already qualified themselves. Aaron had helped make a golden calf not long before this point in the story. Yet God called him. Priesthood was a gift of grace, not a reward for merit. God chooses, and then He equips.

Peter takes this language and applies it to all who belong to Christ: "you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood" (1 Pet 2:9). Every believer now has direct access to God and a calling to represent Him. You do not need special robes or family lineage. If you belong to Jesus, you have been brought out from among and set apart for God's service. That calling did not depend on your qualifications, and your failures do not cancel it. Live today as someone God has chosen and set apart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I see myself as genuinely called and set apart by God?
Am I disqualifying myself from serving God because of my past?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You call people not because they have qualified themselves but because of Your grace. Thank You for setting me apart in Christ. Help me live worthy of that calling. Amen.
